items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And then the Good Father, he came out second. That was Boston Jimmy Sly. Then the Tap Dancers Dream, Bravery -- that was Baby Lawrence, he came out. And then the Godfather was Chuck Green, and I came out fourth over there, okay.

ctx.x: So, we wanted the buck to be the buck, so we accepted. And then it's all beginning to happen, and it's starting out. So, there we come. We got this chance to go down and get orchestrations, and new costumes, and to premier, you know, and then be contracted, you see. And in a way it was, of course -- I think they was going to enlarge it -- this house, see. See, but the tap dancers are being -- they're being

commercialized, you know. Like Sandman got called away on a tour and -- which he always is called away. And the other one, the Good Father, Boston Jimmy Sly, he never could do the Sundays, you know. He had to go back to Massachusetts. And that's where his home is. He had to do his Sundays up there.

That's how I started to call them the on-the-town dancers these names, you see. Good Father and -- well, they liked it see. At least -- because the audience -- it was entertaining to the audience, you see.
